questions.evidence:
[Form rules] Each respondent selected either one or two different workshop topics. Choices were not ranked. Each student submitted exactly one valid form. The center surveyed fifty students and received a response from every one of them.

[Results] Art received thirty selections, Science received twenty-five, and Games received fifteen. These seventy selections came from the fifty respondents. The form did not ask why they chose a topic or which selected topic they liked best.

[Planning note] Art has the largest count, but a session still depends on finding a teacher and room. The center will contact possible teachers before announcing any booking. Interest is evidence for planning, not a promise that a workshop will run.

The team checks both counts and wording before writing its report. It can compare selections and calculate how many people chose two topics, but it cannot invent ranked preferences or reasons absent from the form.
